content.title: About
content.content: Gluten‑free pancakes are light, fluffy discs made from a blend of gluten‑free flours (such as rice, buckwheat or oat), eggs, milk and a touch of oil. They are suitable for people with celiac disease or anyone following a gluten‑free diet while preserving the classic taste and texture of traditional pancakes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Gluten‑free pancakes can be made with a variety of flours, each giving a distinct flavor and color.
The first documented gluten‑free pancake recipe appeared in the 1970s in the United States as gluten‑free diets gained popularity.
They are often served with berry sauces, honey, nut butter, or fresh fruit.
When the liquid‑to‑flour ratio is slightly higher than in regular pancakes, the result is a tender, airy crumb.
Gluten‑free pancakes freeze well; after thawing they can be quickly reheated on a skillet.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Gluten‑free flours contain no gluten, which can irritate the gut of people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and milk provide B12, riboflavin and niacin, essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Good source of protein
items.content: Eggs and milk add complete protein that helps tissue repair and satiety.

items.title: Low glycemic impact
items.content: Using whole‑grain gluten‑free flours like buckwheat helps maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: A small amount of vegetable oil supplies omega‑6 fatty acids important for skin and hair health.

items.title: Egg or dairy allergy
items.content: The pancakes contain eggs and milk, which can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Some recipes add sugar; people monitoring sugar intake should adjust the amount.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Even gluten‑free pancakes are calorie‑dense due to oil and dairy; portion control is recommended.

items.title: Cross‑contamination
items.content: Use clean utensils and surfaces to avoid accidental gluten exposure during preparation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve warm with honey, maple syrup, berry compote, low‑fat yogurt, or cottage cheese. They can be rolled with savory fillings like vegetables, ham or cheese, or used as a base for gluten‑free casseroles.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked pancakes in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze them on parchment‑lined trays; reheat on a skillet or in the microwave before serving.
